status: development pilots only; the held-out registration below is a plan, not a run
hypothesis: For maintenance and incomplete-implementation tasks of the frozen pack, an arm whose prompt names the focused structured context (arm `focused-context`) is not worse than the plain arm at independent behavioural acceptance, and its wall time to accepted completion is no larger by more than the noise floor.

design.unit: one task attempted by one solver session; tasks are the unit of diversity, repeated attempts at one task are not independent
design.pairing: each task is attempted once per arm with identical brief, source snapshot, prompts except the arm note, compiler, cache policy, tools, and wall budget

held_out_sample_size.register_before_first_run: 24 tasks per arm: 12 maintenance and 12 incomplete-implementation tasks, matched within family, so a 3-task difference is detectable at the thresholds below
held_out_sample_size.note: the number is deliberately not fixed here because the development pilots must first establish outcome headroom and variance; it is registered in this file, in a commit that touches nothing else, before the first held-out run

primary_outcome: independent behavioural acceptance within the wall budget, per attempt, as the acceptance checker's exit status and JSON verdict
secondary_outcomes: wall time to accepted completion, with unsuccessful attempts reported separately
failed compiler and test invocations, and repeated diagnostics
unintended changes outside the task's allowed paths
cold, warm-unchanged and warm-after-edit build behaviour with reuse counters

decision_thresholds.useful_improvement: paired pass-rate difference >= 3 of 24 tasks in favour of `focused-context` AND one-sided exact McNemar p <= 0.05 on the discordant pairs
decision_thresholds.correctness_loss: reject the arm if any accepted solution fails an independent re-run of the same hidden oracle, or if its unintended-change rate is above the plain arm's by more than one task
decision_thresholds.latency: reported as median wall time to accepted completion per arm; a latency difference alone never decides the comparison
decision_thresholds.noise_floor: one task (1/24 = 0.042 pass rate) and 5% relative on any latency number

inconclusive_definition: The comparison is inconclusive, and no workflow recommendation may be made, when any of these holds: fewer than 24 paired tasks per arm were run; the discordant pair count is below 6; the observed difference is smaller than the 3-task threshold; the pass rate is at the ceiling (all tasks accepted) or the floor (two or fewer accepted) in both arms, so there is no headroom to detect anything; the two arms' profile_identity or compiler identity differ; or more than one task in either arm was blocked rather than attempted. An inconclusive result is recorded as inconclusive and is not rounded into a direction.
stopping_rule: Run the registered 24 pairs once. Do not extend a cohort because an interim difference looks promising; a larger cohort is a new preregistration.
development_pilot_rule: Development pilots exist to show that the harness runs, that the acceptance check discriminates a correct from an incorrect tree, and to size the variance. They are reported task by task with the solver named, and they are never pooled with a held-out cohort or quoted as a productivity result.
